transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-28
Time: 16:32 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Aisha Patel (Redwood SE), Chris Novak (Redwood Product), Marcus Chen (CTO - NorthStar), Leah Rivera (Head of ML), Omar Diaz (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Security), Ben Hollis (Data Ops)

Summary (auto): Quick console demo — per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, latency and token analytics. Confirm pilot runway and security needs.

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec. Marcus, Leah, thanks for making time. Quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE; Aisha is our SE and she'll run the console demo.
00:21 Marcus Chen: hey thanks, Jordan. We're hoping to see how Redwood will help us with cost visibility across our recommendation and search routes and also how we can get predictable latency for the storefront experiences.
00:35 Aisha Patel: Great — that's exactly what we'll show. We'll go through per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and then touch on Dedicated vs Hosted and VPC options. If at any point you want to jump in, please do.
00:50 Leah Rivera: quick note, our SLA aim is 99.9 p95 latency under 200ms for recommendation ranking calls, with about 150 qps peak per region, and requests are typically 256 tokens input with 64 token expected output.
01:12 Aisha Patel: perfect, that context is super helpful. I'll start screen share — tell me if you can't see it.
01:30 [screen share begins]
01:35 Aisha Patel: OK — this is the Redwood Console home. Top left we have org usage, and on the right there's a quick cost snapshot. I'm going to navigate to Routes -> Per-Route Dashboard.
01:50 Aisha Patel: Here, you can see routes we've instrumented — in your pilot we might have routes like /recommend, /search, /chat-support. Each route has throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost-per-1k-requests, and token breakdown.
02:15 Omar Diaz: is that cost per token or does it include infra overhead?
02:22 Aisha Patel: Good question. The cost number here is unit economics we compute: tokenized usage * model unit price + estimated infra multiplier from running kernels, batching and cache savings applied. You can click into the cost model to see the assumptions.
02:40 [clicks into cost breakdown]
02:45 Aisha Patel: This view shows tokens by input/output, prompt/template amplification, and inferred batching efficiency. Notice these routes had strong KV-cache hits — that's the gray bar. If you enable prefix caching we can lower token generation needs for repeated prefixes.
03:12 Ben Hollis: how accurate is that inferred batching number? our traffic is bursty at midnight restocks.
03:22 Aisha Patel: We infer effective batch sizes from inter-arrival times; it's an estimate but we've seen it model reality within ~10-15% for similar e-commerce patterns. For pilot benchmarking we run a replay to get a ground truth.
03:45 Marcus Chen: you mentioned KV cache — our stack uses Redis for session state, would Redwood's cache layer integrate?
03:54 Aisha Patel: The KV cache here refers to model KV attention cache for autoregressive inference — it's separate. For session-level caching you can use a fronting CDN or edge cache; we also support integrating with existing Redis for higher-level caching. We'll include architecture notes in the docs.
04:15 Jordan Lee: I'm going to pull up the cost simulator — this is a key bit. Jordan switches to the cost simulator view.
04:22 Aisha Patel: The simulator lets us input your traffic profile — qps, average input length, output tokens, and mix of routes. It applies model selection (we show a few variants) and batching assumptions to produce a projected monthly bill and per-call latency estimate.
04:40 Leah Rivera: can we run this per-region? we need US and EU breakdown for data residency cost modeling.
04:48 Aisha Patel: Yes — region toggle up top. You can also model Dedicated capacity with reserved vCPU/GPU and compare against Hosted burst pricing.
05:05 [shows example toggles: model variant, quantization, batch size]
05:12 Aisha Patel: For example, switching from the high-accuracy model to a quantized variant reduces cost by ~37% in this estimate and adds ~20ms to p95 in this demo.
05:30 Omar Diaz: what's the overhead for Dedicated — the reserved GPU pool price vs hosted?
05:36 Jordan Lee: We typically show delta as reserved monthly commit vs on-demand. For your volume, Dedicated with 2x A100-style nodes looks competitive — we'll run exact numbers after you provide token histograms.
05:51 Priya Singh: Security question — do you provide audit logs for per-request data, and how long are logs retained?
05:58 Aisha Patel: Yes — we have per-request audit logs, and retention is configurable per plan. For Private/VPC we can hand control of logs or stream to your SIEM. We'll include SOC2 artifact links in the follow-up.
06:20 [navigates to Audit & Security tab]
06:30 Aisha Patel: Here is the audit logs view; you can filter by route, model, user token, and export to S3 or Splunk. Also show SSO/SAML and RBAC settings.
06:48 Priya Singh: do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM for key wrapping?
06:54 Aisha Patel: Yes, for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, or HSM) — we have a connector.
07:05 Marcus Chen: back to the per-route cost — can you break down by prompt templates? we have many templated prompts for product copy.
07:16 Aisha Patel: Absolutely — the console will show token usage per prompt template tag. We recommend instrumenting templates with IDs so the UI groups them.
07:30 [moves to Alerts/Anomalies view]
07:35 Aisha Patel: This is our anomaly detection: you can create alerts on sudden token spikes or latency regressions. It ties to the quality monitoring in Redwood Optimize if you want automated rollbacks.
07:52 Leah Rivera: are rollbacks automatic? say if a model regression is detected in production on quality evals.
07:59 Aisha Patel: You can configure automatic fallback to a lower-tier model or a canary policy; full auto-rollback is possible but we usually recommend a canary + human-in-the-loop for model quality issues.
08:18 [switches back to per-route details]
08:25 Aisha Patel: Now I'm going to open a single route page — /recommend. You can see time-series for latency, tokens per call, cost per call, and model version rollouts. There's also a token heatmap to spot heavy prompts.
08:45 Ben Hollis: Seeing model version rollout — can we pin certain routes to a specific quantized variant?
08:52 Aisha Patel: Yes. Route-level pinning is supported so you can route /checkout to a higher SLO model and /email-gen to a cheaper quantized model.
09:05 Marcus Chen: how do you handle fallbacks when capacity is constrained? we don't want 503s during peaks.
09:12 Aisha Patel: Smart routing includes fallback policies — route to Dedicated, Hosted, or cheaper model variants. You can set priorities and degrade gracefully; the console shows historical fallback events.
09:28 [scrolling]
09:35 Aisha Patel: Here's the per-token cost waterfall — input token cost, output token cost, model unit price, and infra overhead. You can export per-route CSV for billing reconciliation.
09:48 Omar Diaz: is the infra overhead a fixed multiplier?
09:53 Aisha Patel: It's modeled from observed kernels, sequence lengths, and batching. So not fixed — it adjusts per workload.
10:05 [short pause, attendees murmuring]
10:20 Jordan Lee: We'll run through a quick example calc — assume 150 qps peak, 256 input, 64 output, average 5% cache hit. Aisha, can you toggle the simulator to those numbers?
10:35 Aisha Patel: toggled. The simulator shows monthly token volume of ~1.1B tokens, estimated monthly spend $26k Hosted, $19k Dedicated with our reserved assumptions. Again, these are estimates — we'll run a live replay to confirm.
11:00 Marcus Chen: that Dedicated number looks promising. What's the pilot minimum?
11:07 Jordan Lee: Pilots typically start at a 3-month reserved window with a usage commitment; we can structure a short trial for production-like traffic if you want to validate latency and cost.
11:20 Leah Rivera: for the replay, do you need raw logs or can you give sampled traffic?
11:27 Aisha Patel: Raw logs are best for fidelity but sampled histograms work too. For e-commerce, we prefer 7 days to capture diurnal and restock spikes.
11:40 Priya Singh: From a compliance side, we need to see SOC2 section on data access and deletion — can you include that in the follow-up?
11:48 Aisha Patel: Yes, I'll send SOC2 summary and our data handling doc.
12:02 [switches to API usage analytics]
12:10 Aisha Patel: This page shows top endpoints by cost and latency, plus token-level histograms. You can drill into a request and see the model inference trace — kernel times, KV cache hits, and batching delay.
12:32 Omar Diaz: inference trace — is that safe to export? any PII in the trace?
:12:38 Aisha Patel: Traces are metadata only, not user PII. We redact request bodies in the trace unless you opt-in for debugging; we can stream raw traces to your secure S3 if needed under a private arrangement.
13:00 Chris Novak: quick product note — we recently added per-route negotiated SLAs for Dedicated customers.
13:10 Marcus Chen: good to hear. Any chance to see a demo of the replay tool?
13:18 Aisha Patel: We can run a replay as part of the pilot — we stand up a harness that replays at scale into a dedicated cluster and measure p95, throughput, and cost. We'll share the replay results and a comparison report.
13:40 Leah Rivera: Regarding model variants — do you provide recommended quantization levels or quantized model flavors?
13:47 Aisha Patel: Yes, Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching settings per workload. The console will show recommended profiles with expected SLO impact.
14:05 Jordan Lee: I want to call out billing reconciliation — the exportable CSV includes mapping to your internal product codes so finance can reconcile.
14:18 Ben Hollis: nice. On rate limiting — can we set per-route quotas for bursts to protect other services?
14:25 Aisha Patel: Absolutely — per-route rate limits and quotas are configurable; you can set hard cutoffs or soft throttles with queueing.
14:40 Marcus Chen: what's your typical onboarding time for a pilot?
14:46 Jordan Lee: From contract to Pilot we usually onboard in 2-4 weeks depending on networking and security reviews; for Private deployments it can be longer.
14:58 Priya Singh: Network question — for VPC peering how is traffic egress handled?
15:04 Aisha Patel: For VPC we support private connectivity (VPC peering or private link) and you can keep data plane traffic inside your network for Private deployments; we'll provide a network diagram and ports.
15:20 [Aisha drops a link into chat: SOC2 redacted report (link), network diagram (pdf), pilot checklist]
15:40 Marcus Chen: thanks — we'll review. Any red flags you see with our ask? we want sub-200ms p95.
15:48 Aisha Patel: Based on the numbers you gave, it's achievable with Dedicated + optimized batching and KV cache for hot prefixes. The replay will confirm. We should model worst-case spikes too.
16:05 Jordan Lee: Ok last bits — ops and escalation. Our Dedicated customers get 24/7 support with a named CSM on enterprise tiers; console also provides tracing hooks for your SRE to ingest.
16:22 Marcus Chen: and data residency for EU?
16:26 Aisha Patel: We can pin workloads to EU regions and restrict model routing to those regions; audit logs can be stored in-region.
16:40 [wrap up and recap]
16:45 Jordan Lee: Recap: Jordan will send pilot proposal and pricing; Aisha will send SOC2, network diagram, and pilot checklist; Marcus will provide token histograms/sample logs. We'll target a pilot start in early February.
17:02 Marcus Chen: sounds good, thanks everyone.
17:08 Leah Rivera: appreciated the demo — look forward to the replay and the numbers.
17:15 Jordan Lee: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links and the proposal.
17:22 [call ends]

Notes: transcript has occasional autop-generated artifacts and filler; some technical terms may be slightly garbled (e.g., "KV cache" called out a few ways). Links shared in chat: SOC2 redacted report (link), network diagram (link), pilot checklist (link).
